what: Hyatt Hotels manages and franchises hotels under brands including Park Hyatt, Grand Hyatt, Andaz, Thompson and, after acquiring Playa, a large all-inclusive resort portfolio. It has been selling the hotels it owns to become a fee business.
customers: Hotel owners paying for its brands and management, and business and leisure travellers booking through its system and loyalty programme.
money: fees from hotels it manages or franchises
all-inclusive resort distribution and vacation ownership
moat: A luxury-weighted brand portfolio and the World of Hyatt loyalty programme, which gives owners a booking channel that fills rooms at better rates than they could alone.
risks: It reported a small loss after asset sale and transaction charges
Debt of about $4.6 billion against under $500 million of cash
Travel demand falls in a recession
It is smaller than Marriott and Hilton, which limits loyalty network effects
opportunities: Selling owned hotels converts a capital-heavy business into a fee business
All-inclusive resorts give it a format its larger rivals are weaker in
watch: Net rooms growth and the share of earnings from fees rather than owned hotels.
